messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for customer Thaleia on Dedicated cluster d-3-az2. 5min error rate spike to 18% (baseline ~0.4%). Auto-escalation -> paging P1. Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/reliability/dedicated-5xx

ryan-oncall: on it. joining. can someone paste the top-level error distribution?

maya-sre: Grafana dashboard -> https://grafana.internal/r/dedicated/d-3-az2?orgId=1&panel=errors 5xxs are mostly 502/504 + a burst of gateway timeouts. CPU/GPU on hosts look ok but KV eviction counters jumped. snippet from query: `sum(rate(requests{cluster="d-3-az2",customer="thaleia"}[1m])) by (code)` -> 502: 12.6, 504: 4.1, 200: 70

lin-infra: checked node-level metrics. network retransmits elevated on host gpunode-12, and iostat shows high disk write latency on kv-store pod. likely KV pressure causing backend stalls. kv_evictions_total spiked from 20/min to 450/min over last 10m.

julia-support: customer SRE (Thaleia) says they see timeouts in their app and their retries are amplifying traffic. They asked if we can route them off d-3-az2 temporarily.

ryan-oncall: plan: 1) apply temporary routing weight 0 for thaleia on d-3-az2 (drain traffic) 2) patch autoscaler to bump dedicated pool (if available) 3) investigate noisy tenant processes on gpunode-12 4) keep customer informed. executing step 1 now.

maya-sre: +1. also enable prefix-KV hot-cache bypass for Thaleia to reduce write amplification. quick command to remove routing: `redwoodctl route update --cluster d-3-az2 --customer thaleia --weight 0 --reason "emergency drain"`

harpreet-ops: running redwoodctl now. output: ```
# redwoodctl route update
INFO updating route for thaleia on d-3-az2 -> weight 0
OK propagated to gateway pool (3/3 nodes)
```

incident-bot: NOTE: Automated fallback applied: traffic rerouted to cluster d-1-az1 and d-2-az3. Error rate for Thaleia on d-3-az2 dropping in tail-end requests but customer still impacted via other clusters (increased latency).

lin-infra: investigating gpunode-12: top shows a single tenant container `thaleia-worker-evictor` consuming high async IO; suspect a background compaction job. pid 2378 showing high iowait and lock contention on /mnt/kv. I'll isolate the pod.

ryan-oncall: isolation steps? we can cordon the node or evict the pod. prefer targeted eviction to avoid broad customer impact. maya, can we throttle that tenant process?

maya-sre: issuing eviction for that pod: `kubectl delete pod thaleia-worker-evictor-2378 -n dedicated-thaleia --grace-period=30` will trigger restart into another node. also adding QoS patch to lower IO priority for restart.

harpreet-ops: eviction succeeded. pod restarted on gpunode-18. iostat shows write latency normalized on gpunode-12. kv_evictions_total trending down.

julia-support: notified Thaleia SRE: "We've drained your traffic from d-3-az2 and evicted a noisy background job. We're monitoring; please verify your retries are stable." They replied: "Seeing improvement on our end, thanks. Still some 504s on long-tail requests though."

maya-sre: long-tail 504s likely due to in-flight KV cache inconsistency after eviction. Flushing prefix cache for Thaleia should help: `redis-cli -h cache-d3 flushkey thaleia:*` (run carefully). I'll run against staging mirror first.

lin-infra: runbook step executed: flushed mirror cache -> no regressions, then performed production flush with rate-limit.

incident-bot: ALERT: autoscaler suggested +2 GPUs for dedicated pool d-3. Manual approve needed for burst. Current reserve usage 92%.

ryan-oncall: approving +2 GPUs burst for 30m. harpreet please kick off.

harpreet-ops: provisioning started. ETA ~6m.\nProvisioning logs:
```
provision -> allocate g4dn.xlarge x2
attach to pool d-3
configure routing weights
```

ryan-oncall: monitoring metrics. 5xx for Thaleia overall dropping from 18% -> 3.2% over 12m since drain + eviction + burst. latency p95 still elevated (1.8s -> 1.2s).

maya-sre: root cause hypothesis: Thaleia's compaction/job created sustained KV write pressure causing evictions and increased KV tail latency, which surfaced as 502/504 gateway errors during our short tail retry storms. Mitigation applied: drain, evict noisy job, flush caches, burst capacity. Next: follow-up to add per-tenant IO cgroups + throttling and adjust autoscaler thresholds for KV pressure signal.

julia-support: customer impact summary for post-incident ticket: "Thaleia experienced elevated 5xx and timeouts from 12:08-12:42 UTC caused by tenant KV write pressure on Dedicated cluster d-3-az2. Immediate mitigations: traffic drained off d-3-az2, noisy job evicted and restarted, prefix cache flushed, and +2 GPU burst provisioned. Errors returned to baseline by 12:36 UTC; p95 latency improved but still under review. No data loss reported."

ryan-oncall: creating incident report in Jira: RDW-INC-2026-1392. tagging eng-ml, infra, and product for follow-up. handing off to maya for postmortem and remediation tasks.

maya-sre: taking postmortem. initial action items: 1) add tenant IO throttle and cgroup policies (owner: infra) 2) add KV-eviction alert that ties into autoscaler (owner: eng-ml) 3) validate runbook steps for targeted eviction vs cordon (owner: sops) 4) follow up with Thaleia on retry/backoff guidance (owner: support).

harpreet-ops: removing burst capacity in 30m window unless metrics disagree.

ryan-oncall: thanks team. closing active paging channel in 10m unless new alerts. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident marked: mitigated. Timeline and data preserved at https://incidents.internal/4998765432
